items.title: Turkish Ambassador Ferhat Alkan meets former Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire
items.summary: Türkiye's Ambassador to Somalia, Ferhat Alkan, held a courtesy meeting with Hassan Ali Khaire, Somalia's 19th Prime Minister. They discussed the country's political process, the efforts of the Quartet of Türkiye, the United States, the United Kingdom and the European Union, and relations between Türkiye and Somalia.
items.imageAlt: Turkish Ambassador Ferhat Alkan (left) and former Somali Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire (right) standing side by side, with Somali flags behind them

items.title: IGAD's Somalia representative receives Sweden's ambassador in Mogadishu
items.summary: IGAD's Representative to Somalia, Mohamud Karshe, received Sweden's Ambassador to Somalia, H.E. Amb. Hans Henric Lundquist, at the IGAD office in Mogadishu, where they discussed strengthening cooperation on peace, security and stability.
items.imageAlt: IGAD Representative to Somalia Mohamud Karshe and Swedish Ambassador Hans Henric Lundquist at the IGAD office in Mogadishu

items.title: England women cancel West Indies Test to prepare for the Ashes
items.summary: England's women's cricket team have cancelled a Test that was due to be played in the West Indies in April and will instead play red-ball matches in England to prepare for the Ashes, BBC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: A building at Headingley cricket ground in Leeds, England

items.title: Somalia's justice minister warns of threat to statehood, calls for review of federal system
items.summary: Somalia's Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Hassan Macallin Mohamud, warned on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, of the political and security dangers facing the country and called for the federal system to be reviewed, Hiiraan Online reported.
items.imageAlt: Politicians and Somali elders at Villa Somalia during the signing of the Baidoa federal state agreement (2014 photo)

items.title: Trump's envoys head to Moscow to see Putin after Abu Dhabi talks end without clear progress
items.summary: Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law, said on Wednesday that he and Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff would travel to Moscow tomorrow to meet President Vladimir Putin, after trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a clear breakthrough, CNN reported.
items.imageAlt: Russian President Vladimir Putin shaking hands with US envoy Steve Witkoff, 5 September 2026

items.title: Spain holds its first general strike in 14 years over the housing crisis
items.summary: Millions of workers in Spain began a 24-hour general strike on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, demanding that the government tackle the housing crisis, less than three weeks before the 29 November national election, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Posters calling for the general strike of 14 November 2012 on a street in Barcelona (archive photo)

items.title: Kenya discharges its last Ebola patient, starting a 42-day countdown to being declared free of the disease
items.summary: Kenya on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, discharged its last Ebola patient from hospital, beginning a 42-day monitoring period; if no new cases are found, the country will be declared Ebola-free on 23 December, Health Minister Aden Duale said.
items.imageAlt: Aden Duale, then Kenya's Defence Cabinet Secretary, speaking at Manda Bay, September 2023

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh and Prime Minister Abiy discuss the security of Somalia and the region in Türkiye
items.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed met in Türkiye ahead of the COP31 leaders' summit in the city of Antalya and discussed the security situation in Somalia and developments in the Horn of Africa, Ethiopian state media outlet Fana reported.
items.imageAlt: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed at the inauguration ceremony of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in Mogadishu, June 2022

items.title: Somaliland executes nine prisoners sentenced to death by its courts for murder
items.summary: The Somaliland administration on Wednesday morning, 11 November 2026, carried out death sentences in the Mandheera area on nine people whom Somaliland's courts had earlier sentenced to death after convicting them of murder, Hiiraan Online reported.
items.imageAlt: The war memorial in central Hargeisa, the capital of Somaliland (photo 2007)

items.title: Somalia and Saudi Arabia sign 2027 Hajj agreement: Somalia allocated 11,500 pilgrims
items.summary: The Federal Government of Somalia and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia signed the Hajj quota agreement for the year 1448 AH (2027) in Jeddah, allocating Somalia 11,500 pilgrims, Goobjoog News reported.
items.imageAlt: Somalia's Minister of Endowments and Religious Affairs, Sheikh Mukhtar Robow Ali, attending a conference in Mogadishu, January 2023

items.title: Lithuania closes Vilnius and Kaunas airports and NATO scrambles jets after drones from Belarus
items.summary: NATO fighter jets were scrambled twice overnight after suspected drones believed to have come from Belarus triggered air alerts across large parts of Lithuania, and the Vilnius and Kaunas airports were temporarily closed, Türkiye Today reported, citing Lithuanian public broadcaster LRT.
items.imageAlt: The main entrance of Vilnius International Airport, Lithuania

items.title: US formally confirms its troops have left Baledogle base
items.summary: US Africa Command (AFRICOM) has for the first time formally confirmed that US troops have left the Baledogle military base in the Lower Shabelle region after its runway deteriorated, Hiiraan Online reported.
items.imageAlt: US troops and the Danab brigade training at Baledogle base, April 2021

items.title: Heads of security agencies meet opposition leaders in Mogadishu
items.summary: The commanders of Somalia's security and military agencies have met opposition leaders in Mogadishu in talks focused on the country's security situation and political tension, Hiiraan Online reported.
items.imageAlt: Former prime minister Mohamed Hussein Roble speaking at a conference in Mogadishu, December 2020

items.title: Senator Ted Cruz ties support for new US ambassador to Somalia to the Somaliland question
items.summary: US Senator Ted Cruz has said his support for confirming Devin Kennington, whom President Donald Trump nominated as US ambassador to Somalia, depends on how the administration acts on the president's position on Somaliland, Hiiraan Online reported.
items.imageAlt: Senator Ted Cruz, official US Senate portrait (2019)

items.title: Uganda and East African lawyers' bodies urge Hassan Sheikh to respect Supreme Court
items.summary: The Uganda Law Society and the East Africa Law Society (EALS) called on President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in statements issued on 10 November 2026 to respect the rulings of Somalia's Supreme Court, Hiiraan Online and Puntland Post reported.
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud giving a speech in Mogadishu (2012 photo)

items.title: Tanzania: TANAPA national parks revenue triples in five years
items.summary: The Tanzania National Parks Authority (TANAPA) says its revenue rose from 174 billion shillings in 2021/2022 to 534 billion shillings in 2025/2026, while the number of tourists passed 1.5 million.
items.imageAlt: A wild lion in Serengeti National Park, Tanzania

items.title: Piracy off Somalia's coast on the rise again as fishermen in Bandar Beyla complain
items.summary: Pirate attacks off Somalia's coast have been increasing again since April 2026, according to a report published on 10 November by Africa Defense Forum, raising concern over the safety of merchant ships in the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.
items.imageAlt: A boat used by Somali pirates, seized by the Finnish navy during Operation Atalanta

items.title: Kenya: Senate committee concerned over Kasarani stadium's readiness for AFCON 2027
items.summary: The Kenyan Senate's Committee on Labour and Social Welfare has raised concerns over the readiness of the Moi International Sports Centre, Kasarani, which is due to host matches at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON).
items.imageAlt: Inside Kasarani stadium (Moi International Sports Centre), Nairobi, Kenya

items.title: Ebola: cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo pass 11,000, with 5,387 deaths
items.summary: The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 11,042, with at least 5,387 deaths, according to government data released on Tuesday.
items.imageAlt: Congolese Red Cross volunteers in Bunia, Ituri province, during the Ebola outbreak, August 2026

items.title: Russia says it downed 146 drones over the Leningrad region
items.summary: The governor of Russia's Leningrad region, Aleksandr Drozdenko, said 146 drones were shot down during an attack on the region on Tuesday, according to Russia's state news agency TASS.
items.imageAlt: The office of the KINEF oil refining company in the town of Kirishi, Leningrad region

items.title: El Salvador says it destroyed the headquarters of the 400 Mawozo gang in Haiti
items.summary: El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele said his country's military destroyed the headquarters of the 400 Mawozo gang, one of Haiti's largest criminal gangs, in a ground and air attack on a complex on the outskirts of the capital Port-au-Prince, the BBC reported.
items.imageAlt: Port-au-Prince, the capital of Haiti, seen from above

items.title: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah back in court today, facing possible prison
items.summary: Prominent Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, head of the independent media outlet Mada Masr, appears on Wednesday before a criminal court for a retrial on charges of operating without a licence and publishing false news, France 24 reported.
items.imageAlt: Lina Attalah, head of Mada Masr, speaking at the International Journalism Festival in Perugia, Italy, 2024

items.title: UNCTAD: climate change could wipe 10% off global output
items.summary: The UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) has warned that the economic losses from climate change could reach about 10% of world gross domestic product if global temperatures rise by 3 degrees Celsius, Türkiye Today reported.
items.imageAlt: Rebeca Grynspan, UNCTAD Secretary-General, at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, 2021

items.title: Eric Zemmour announces he will run for the French presidency a second time
items.summary: French far-right author and politician Eric Zemmour confirmed on Tuesday on TF1 television that he will be a candidate in next year's presidential election, Al Jazeera reported, citing the AFP news agency.
items.imageAlt: Eric Zemmour, the French far-right politician, April 2022

items.title: Russia expels a Moldovan diplomat in response to a move by Chisinau
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday it had expelled a staff member of Moldova's embassy, describing it as a response to Moldova's decision to expel an employee of the Russian embassy, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: The headquarters of Russia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Moscow

items.title: Erdoğan holds six meetings at COP31 as Türkiye and Saudi Arabia sign power deal
items.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on Tuesday received six leaders and officials in Antalya, where the COP31 climate conference is under way, and witnessed the signing of an electricity memorandum of understanding between Türkiye and Saudi Arabia.
items.imageAlt: Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar

items.title: US House begins a vote deciding the fate of the resolution to impeach Hegseth
items.summary: The US House of Representatives on Tuesday began a procedural vote to decide whether the resolution to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth is sent back to committee or moves to a final vote, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: The US House of Representatives chamber in the Capitol, Washington

items.title: Gianni Infantino could be summoned by the US Congress in January
items.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino may have to respond to subpoenas issued by the US Congress in the coming weeks, probably in January, according to the British newspaper The Telegraph.
items.imageAlt: FIFA President Gianni Infantino

items.title: UNIFIL peacekeepers come under fire while on patrol in southern Lebanon
items.summary: The United Nations peacekeeping force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) said on Tuesday that about 12 rounds were fired at one of its patrols near Wadi Jilu in the Tyre district, without naming who was responsible.
items.imageAlt: A UNIFIL peacekeeper on patrol along the Blue Line in southern Lebanon

items.title: Tanzania says it spent 604.6 billion shillings building 676 schools over the past 5 years
items.summary: Tanzania's Deputy Minister of State for Regional Administration and Local Government, Dr Festo Dugange, said the government spent 604.6 billion shillings on building 676 new schools and 34,464 latrines, the state-owned Daily News reported.
items.imageAlt: Pupils at Nyakahoja Primary School in Mwanza city, Tanzania

items.title: US soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of spying for Russia
items.summary: London's counter-terrorism police say a 41-year-old member of the US military was arrested near the city of Gloucester on suspicion of breaching national security law in connection with Russia.
items.imageAlt: The New Scotland Yard sign at the Metropolitan Police headquarters in London

items.title: Lewis Hamilton visits the Egypt-Gaza border to see humanitarian aid efforts
items.summary: Formula 1 driver Lewis Hamilton, a 7-time world champion, on Tuesday visited the Egyptian city of El Arish and the Rafah crossing, where he met aid workers preparing assistance for the Gaza Strip.
items.imageAlt: Formula 1 driver Lewis Hamilton

items.title: Aurélien Tchouaméni leaves the France squad with an injury
items.summary: Real Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni is leaving the France camp after an injury in the groin area and will miss the UEFA Nations League matches against Italy and Turkey, RMC Sport and L'Équipe reported.
items.imageAlt: Aurélien Tchouaméni playing for the France national team

items.title: Trump administration proposes rule that could remove 6.3 million people from food aid
items.summary: The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) on Tuesday published a proposed rule ending automatic eligibility for the SNAP programme, which Al Jazeera reported could remove about 6.3 million people.
items.imageAlt: A farmers' market in Baltimore where EBT food aid cards are accepted

items.title: Kirk Cousins returns to the Minnesota Vikings as the Raiders hand the job to Fernando Mendoza
items.summary: The Minnesota Vikings acquired 38-year-old quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a round 3 pick in the 2027 draft, The Athletic and The Guardian reported.
items.imageAlt: Kirk Cousins in a Minnesota Vikings uniform during an NFL game

items.title: Jim Jordan elected Republican leader in the US House after the party lost its majority
items.summary: Republican members of the US House of Representatives elected Jim Jordan of Ohio, a close ally of President Donald Trump, in a secret ballot to replace Mike Johnson, a week after the party lost its majority in the midterm elections.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of Congressman Jim Jordan

items.title: US prosecutors: Kataib Hezbollah commander directed plot against UK air base from New York jail
items.summary: A new indictment from US federal prosecutors accuses Mohammad Dawood Al-Saadi, a dual Iranian and Iraqi citizen, of directing a failed plot to attack the RAF Fairford air base in Britain while he was held in a New York jail.
items.imageAlt: A US military aircraft taking off from RAF Fairford in Britain

items.title: Uganda's local government minister orders arrest of officials in Ibanda district
items.summary: Uganda's Minister for Local Government, Balaam Barugahara, has ordered the arrest and suspension of several Ibanda district local government officials accused of corruption, mismanagement of public funds and abuse of office, Nile Post reported.
items.imageAlt: Ugandan minister Balaam Barugahara

items.title: Britain says caretaker government arrangements have weakened South Sudan's political consensus
items.summary: Britain's Deputy Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Kate Foster, told a Security Council meeting in New York that the new caretaker government arrangements have further weakened political consensus, while key provisions of the 2018 peace agreement remain unimplemented, Eye Radio reported.
items.imageAlt: The United Nations Security Council chamber in New York

items.title: Violence in Bangladesh as supporters of Sheikh Hasina stage protests
items.summary: Police in Bangladesh used tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse supporters of deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina who are demanding her return to the country, the BBC reported.
items.imageAlt: The new municipal market in Gopalganj district, Bangladesh

items.title: Von der Leyen pledges 50 million euros to Bulgaria and Romania after Black Sea attacks
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen pledged 50 million euros to speed up a joint maritime security hub that Bulgaria and Romania are setting up in the Black Sea, after drone attacks on cargo ships.
items.imageAlt: The port of Varna in Bulgaria, on the Black Sea coast

items.title: Uganda targets annual production of 210 million pairs of medical gloves
items.summary: Uganda's Minister of State for Industry, David Bahati, commissioned the 2nd production line of the East African Medical Vitals factory in Namanve, which is expected to raise annual capacity from about 80 million to 210 million pairs, Nile Post reported.
items.imageAlt: Medical gloves being tested

items.title: Iran says it has not suspended its NPT commitments, as hardliners talk of a nuclear bomb
items.summary: Iran says it has not suspended its obligations under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), but broad international inspections of its sites remain far off, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: The Bushehr nuclear power plant in Iran

items.title: Appeals court in London strikes down Trinidad and Tobago's ban on gay sex
items.summary: Trinidad and Tobago's final court of appeal, which sits in England, on Tuesday struck down a centuries-old law that criminalised sex between people of the same sex, ABC News reported.
items.imageAlt: Middlesex Guildhall in London, where the court sits

items.title: Scott McTominay reveals he had heart treatment during the World Cup
items.summary: Napoli and Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay said he received treatment to correct an irregular heartbeat two days before Scotland's World Cup win over Haiti in June, BBC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: Scott McTominay playing for Scotland against Bolivia, June 2026

items.title: National Rally reaches preliminary deal with banks to fund Le Pen's campaign
items.summary: France's far-right National Rally party has reached a preliminary agreement with two European banks for a 10.6 million euro loan to fund Marine Le Pen's presidential campaign, the party's treasurer said.
items.imageAlt: Marine Le Pen, leader of the National Rally, in May 2024

items.title: Egypt says its troops have been in Saudi Arabia for months for defensive purposes
items.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said Egyptian soldiers have been stationed in Saudi Arabia for several months to protect key sites after attacks on the kingdom, adding that those forces will not move into Yemen.
items.imageAlt: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty

items.title: South Sudan confirms a fatal yellow fever case in Morobo County
items.summary: South Sudan's Ministry of Health has confirmed that a 48-year-old farmer from Morobo County in Central Equatoria State died of yellow fever after a trip to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Radio Tamazuj reported.
items.imageAlt: Lujule Mountain in Morobo County, South Sudan

items.title: Pochettino reportedly interested in leaving the US national team for Manchester United
items.summary: US men's national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino is interested in taking the Manchester United job, and the interest is mutual, several sources told The Guardian.
items.imageAlt: Mauricio Pochettino leading the US team against Belgium, March 2026

items.title: Uganda's Parliament orders two-week probe into Dei BioPharma investment
items.summary: Uganda's Speaker of Parliament, Jacob Oboth, has directed the science and technology committee to investigate within two weeks the government's 723.4 billion shilling investment in the company Dei BioPharma, Nile Post reported.
items.imageAlt: The Parliament of Uganda building in Kampala

items.title: Kenya moves its Haiti mission to Mexico City
items.summary: Kenya's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said its diplomatic office in Port-au-Prince has been relocated to Mexico City as part of a restructuring of the country's missions abroad, Capital FM reported.
items.imageAlt: Kenya's Foreign Affairs Principal Secretary Korir Sing'oei at a meeting in Vienna

items.title: Eli Junior Kroupi earns first France call-up as Marcus Thuram's replacement
items.summary: Bournemouth's 20-year-old striker Eli Junior Kroupi has been called up to the France squad for the first time by coach Zinédine Zidane, replacing the injured Marcus Thuram, RMC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: Eli Junior Kroupi playing for Bournemouth against Fulham, May 2026

items.title: General Muhoozi deactivates his X account after threatening Uganda's Vice President
items.summary: Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has deactivated his X account after posts in which he threatened Vice President Jessica Alupo with removal from office, The Citizen newspaper reported.
items.imageAlt: Ugandan Vice President Jessica Alupo

items.title: Formula 1 to end the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi as planned
items.summary: Formula 1 has told Italy's Imola circuit it will not be needed as a back-up, with the Qatar (27 to 29 November) and Abu Dhabi (4 to 6 December) races going ahead as planned despite the ongoing conflict between the United States and Israel and Iran, BBC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: Aircraft flying over Yas Island during the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix

items.title: French police make arrests in Mohamed Al Fayed investigation
items.summary: French police made arrests after searching three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, as part of the investigation into the abuse attributed to Mohamed Al Fayed, according to a letter London's Metropolitan Police sent to survivors, reported by the BBC.
items.imageAlt: The Ritz hotel on Place Vendôme in Paris

items.title: TAZARA suspends trains between Mbeya and Makambako until 1 December
items.summary: The Tanzania-Zambia Railway Authority (TAZARA) has suspended passenger and cargo train services between Mbeya and Makambako until 1 December 2026, after a cargo train accident damaged several kilometres of track, the state-owned Daily News reported.
items.imageAlt: A TAZARA train bound for Mbeya

items.title: Uganda says it will lift the suspension of some NGOs
items.summary: Uganda's Minister of Internal Affairs, Ephraim Kamuntu, said non-governmental organisations found to have addressed the concerns raised against them will be allowed to resume operations, after a review of 10 suspended organisations, Nile Post reported.
items.imageAlt: Kampala Road in Uganda's capital, Kampala

items.title: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than expected
items.summary: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October from the previous month, while economists had expected 0.3%, according to data released on Tuesday by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
items.imageAlt: The Postal Square Building in Washington, D.C., home of the US Bureau of Labor Statistics

items.title: Hegseth calls effort to impeach him a farce and sabotage
items.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told a press conference on Tuesday that the House impeachment resolution against him is a farce and a political stunt, calling the criticism of him and of the war on Iran policy disagreements, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth

items.title: OCHA: Somalia's 2026 aid plan has received $300 million, only 35.2% of what is needed
items.summary: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said Somalia's 2026 humanitarian response plan has received about $300 million, which is 35.2 percent of the money required, Goobjoog News reported.
items.imageAlt: Somali women queue for free medical check-ups at a camp for displaced people in Mogadishu

items.title: Usman Khawaja says an MCC member racially abused him at Lord's in 2023
items.summary: Former Australia cricketer Usman Khawaja says in his new autobiography that a Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) member racially abused him during the Ashes Test at Lord's in 2023, BBC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: The Pavilion at Lord's Cricket Ground in London

items.title: Anthropic plans to raise up to $64bn in Nasdaq stock market listing
items.summary: AI company Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, said it will offer its shares at between $70 and $78 each when it lists on New York's Nasdaq exchange, potentially raising up to $64bn, the BBC reported.
items.imageAlt: The Nasdaq MarketSite in New York

items.title: Israel's new parliament sworn in as Eisenkot tries to form a government
items.summary: Members of Israel's new Knesset were sworn in on Tuesday, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to form a government that would oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the BBC reported.
items.imageAlt: The Knesset building, Israel's parliament, in Jerusalem

items.title: Minister Daahir Shire says in Beledweyne the government understands Hiiraan residents' grievances
items.summary: Somalia's Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources, Daahir Shire Mohamed, leading a delegation that arrived in Beledweyne today, said the federal government understands the grievances of the people of the Hiiraan region and will take part in resolving them, Hiiraan Online reported.
items.imageAlt: The town of Beledweyne in the Hiiraan region

items.title: Somali government welcomes 171 citizens returned from Libya
items.summary: Somalia's Federal Government today welcomed 171 citizens who were returned home after earlier migrating irregularly to Libya, Hiiraan Online reported.
items.imageAlt: Aden Abdulle International Airport in Mogadishu

items.title: Turkish ambassador and Somalia's National Security Adviser discuss military and security cooperation
items.summary: Turkey's ambassador to Somalia, Ferhat Alkan, met National Security Adviser Aweys Haji Yusuf Ahmed in Mogadishu to discuss military and security cooperation between the two countries and the fight against terrorism, the Turkish embassy said.
items.imageAlt: Turkey's military base in Mogadishu

items.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guard: two oil tankers on fire in the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The navy of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said that on Tuesday two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after an explosion on a route Iran had not authorised.
items.imageAlt: The Strait of Hormuz seen from an aircraft

items.title: Brent oil price falls below 90 dollars for the first time since August
items.summary: Brent crude fell below 90 dollars a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since August, after President Donald Trump signalled that the conflict with Iran could end, Türkiye Today reported.
items.imageAlt: An oil production platform in the North Sea

items.title: Malaysian court allows Najib Razak to be moved to house arrest
items.summary: The Kuala Lumpur High Court has ruled that former Malaysian prime minister Najib Razak, 73, will serve the rest of his reduced 6-year sentence under house arrest, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Najib Razak, former prime minister of Malaysia, in 2017

items.title: RC Lens sack coach Yannick Cahuzac 2 months after his appointment
items.summary: French top-flight club Lens dismissed head coach Yannick Cahuzac on Tuesday after a week with 3 consecutive defeats, L'Équipe and RMC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: Yannick Cahuzac in 2019

items.title: Japan to give the Philippines coastal radar and drones worth 4.3 billion yen
items.summary: Japan and the Philippines signed a grant agreement in Manila worth 4.3 billion yen (24 million euros), under which Japan will supply the Philippine military with a coastal radar system and drones to monitor shipping, Euronews reported.
items.imageAlt: The Philippine Navy warship BRP Miguel Malvar

items.title: Bulgaria: at least 11 killed in multi-vehicle crash near Yambol
items.summary: At least 11 people were killed and 48 injured in a crash involving many vehicles on the Trakia motorway near the town of Yambol in Bulgaria, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.
items.imageAlt: The Trakia motorway in Bulgaria

items.title: Uganda launches nationwide emergency training to care for injured people
items.summary: A national programme to teach health workers, ambulance crews and ordinary citizens how to respond to people with injuries is being launched in Uganda to reduce preventable deaths, Nile Post reported.
items.imageAlt: An ambulance at work in Kampala

items.title: Iran denies planned talks after Trump says the war is 'effectively over' militarily
items.summary: President Donald Trump said the war with Iran is 'effectively over' militarily, while Iranian officials denied reports of planned talks to be held in Qatar, Euronews reported.
items.imageAlt: Abbas Araghchi at a meeting in Vienna (2021)

items.title: Six countries and companies including Anthropic, OpenAI and Microsoft sign the 'Paris Call' on AI safety
items.summary: The leaders of Bahrain, Canada, Finland, France, Norway and the Netherlands and the heads of 10 AI companies signed a joint declaration called the 'Paris Call for AI Safety and Security' on 9 November, Türkiye Today reported.
items.imageAlt: The Élysée Palace in Paris, seat of the French presidency

items.title: President Samia travels to Antalya to attend the COP31 climate summit
items.summary: Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan has travelled to Antalya in Türkiye to attend the COP31 summit and a high-level meeting on clean cooking in Africa, the government newspaper Daily News reported.
items.imageAlt: Samia Suluhu Hassan (2017)

items.title: Mandera: 8 people killed in an attack on a vehicle guarding workers on the Arabia road
items.summary: At least 8 people were killed when gunmen ambushed a security vehicle guarding workers on the Mandera–Arabia–Lafey road project, The Standard and other Kenyan media reported.
items.imageAlt: The town of Mandera in north-eastern Kenya

items.title: Soldiers from the Hawadle clan leave government forces after a call by the clan's Ugaas
items.summary: At least 300 soldiers from the Hawadle clan have left the ranks of Somalia's federal government forces over the past two days, after an appeal by the clan's paramount Ugaas, Radio Daljir reported.
items.imageAlt: A pick-up truck carrying Somali National Army soldiers drives through Beledweyne (file photo, 2012)

items.title: India: 3 workers die at Tata's iPhone parts plant in Hosur
items.summary: Three contract workers died at the Tata Electronics plant in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, after inhaling gas while inspecting a water-filtration tank, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Sunrise over the city of Hosur, Tamil Nadu, India

items.title: Spain: police officer killed by backpack explosion in the city of Oviedo
items.summary: An officer of Spain's National Police was killed and another seriously injured when a backpack exploded in a building in the city of Oviedo, the BBC and Spanish media reported.
items.imageAlt: A view of the city of Oviedo, Spain

items.title: Uganda: Cabinet approves Shs19 billion for 1,841 traders hit by floods
items.summary: Uganda's Cabinet has approved Shs18.9995 billion in assistance for 1,841 verified traders whose businesses were damaged by the Kampala floods of October 2025, Nile Post reported.
items.imageAlt: St. Balikuddembe (Owino) market in Kampala

items.title: Franziska Liebhardt, gold medallist at the Rio 2016 Paralympics, dies aged 44
items.summary: German athlete Franziska Liebhardt, who won gold in the shot put and silver in the long jump at the Rio 2016 Paralympics, has died aged 44, kicker reported.
items.imageAlt: Franziska Liebhardt (2012)

items.title: US moves aircraft out of Britain's RAF Mildenhall base after a threat from Iran
items.summary: US forces on Monday moved refuelling aircraft out of the RAF Mildenhall air base in eastern England after a reported threat from Iran, according to The Wall Street Journal.
items.imageAlt: A KC-135 refuelling aircraft at RAF Mildenhall

items.title: Kenya: High Court to hear new challenge against Ruto's Cabinet on 1 December
items.summary: Kenya's High Court has certified as urgent an application seeking to suspend the Cabinet, with civil society groups saying President William Ruto has not complied with a court order on reconstituting it.
items.imageAlt: William Ruto speaking at the IAEA General Conference in Vienna (2010)

items.title: beIN Sports apologises after a sexist on-air remark about Sabalenka
items.summary: beIN Sports has apologised after one of its commentators, who thought he was off air, made an offensive remark about Aryna Sabalenka before her WTA Finals match, RMC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: Aryna Sabalenka at the 2025 Miami Open

items.title: Research: fossil fuel emissions set to fall for the first time since Covid
items.summary: Carbon emissions from burning oil, gas and coal are expected to fall by 0.4 percent in 2026, according to the annual Global Carbon Budget report.
items.imageAlt: The smokestacks of the Edwards coal-fired power plant in Illinois, United States

items.title: UN Security Council to hear a briefing today on South Sudan's political and security situation
items.summary: The UN Security Council is holding an open meeting this Tuesday on the political and security situation in South Sudan, Eye Radio reported.

items.title: Ukraine, Russia and US talks resume in Abu Dhabi after a 9-month pause

items.title: Trump: A new strike on Iran would be about five times bigger than the first
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that a new strike on Iran would be roughly five times bigger than the first one, but that he is holding off at the request of Qatar, Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states, Türkiye Today reported.
items.imageAlt: Donald Trump meets Qatar's Emir and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani (2025)

items.title: Ruto launches a 1.3 billion shilling road in Bonchari and announces a 22 billion shilling roads plan

items.title: German court upholds revocation of Somali woman's asylum after visits to Somaliland
items.summary: The Administrative Court in the German city of Trier has rejected an appeal by a Somali woman living in Mainz and upheld the decision of the BAMF migration agency to revoke her refugee status, after videos she posted on TikTok showed she had visited Somaliland several times, Hiiraan Online reported.

items.title: British author M. John Harrison, 81, wins the Booker Prize

items.title: Ramla Ali wins two world boxing title belts

items.title: Bunny Shaw among five contenders for BBC Women's Footballer of the Year 2026
items.summary: The BBC has opened voting for the Women's Footballer of the Year 2026, with a final shortlist of Temwa Chawinga, Ewa Pajor, Alexia Putellas, Alessia Russo and Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw.

items.summary: Thousands of people marched through central Krakow on Monday night in memory of those killed in Saturday's shooting in the Main Market Square, led by President Karol Nawrocki and Prime Minister Donald Tusk, the BBC reported.

items.summary: Australian airline Qantas said 850 office jobs will be outsourced to consulting firm Accenture, most of them moving to India, as it speeds up investment in AI, the BBC reported.

items.summary: Greek Cypriot leader Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman have agreed to open two new crossings across the line that divides the island, Al Jazeera reported.

items.title: Arsène Wenger nears final decision on challenging Infantino in FIFA election
items.summary: Arsène Wenger, the former Arsenal manager, is close to a final decision on whether to run for FIFA president against Gianni Infantino, with his FIFA employment contract expiring at the end of this year, The Athletic reported.

items.title: Lauren Boebert loses her seat in Congress, CNN projects
items.summary: Republican Representative Lauren Boebert has lost the election in Colorado's 4th district, which was won by Eileen Laubacher, a Democrat and former US Navy officer, CNN's Decision Desk projected.

items.title: US Supreme Court allows Trump to continue building the Big Bend border wall in Texas
items.summary: The US Supreme Court has lifted a lower court order that halted construction of the border wall and related infrastructure in the Big Bend region of Texas while the case continues, CNN and CBS News reported.

items.title: US adds Somalia to the 23 countries under its Level 4 travel warning
items.summary: The US State Department said in a notice issued on Monday, 9 November, that Somalia is among 23 countries placed under its highest travel warning, Level 4 "Do Not Travel", Caasimada Online and Eye Radio reported.

items.summary: At least 16 people were killed and 13 others injured in an explosion on Monday at midday at the Habaş steel plant in the Aliağa district, north of the city of Izmir, Turkish officials said; President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announced an investigation.
items.imageAlt: General view of the Aliağa district in Izmir province, Turkey

items.title: South Africa detains 9 foreigners suspected of heading to join Russian forces
items.summary: South African police say nine foreign nationals aged between 20 and 26 were arrested at OR Tambo airport in Johannesburg and a nearby hotel on suspicion of travelling to Russia to fight in the war in Ukraine, Al Jazeera and AP reported.

items.title: Holstein Kiel sack head coach Tim Walter
items.summary: Holstein Kiel have dismissed their head coach Tim Walter, 51, after just one win in 11 matches left the club bottom of the 2. Bundesliga, the official Bundesliga website reported.

items.title: England wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso out of the rest of the Nations Championship
items.summary: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, 23, will miss the rest of the Nations Championship after an ankle injury sustained in England's 45-22 win over Australia, BBC Sport reported. England will also be without Seb Atkinson, Ollie Chessum and George Furbank for Saturday's match against Japan.
items.imageAlt: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso playing for England in Rome, 2024

items.title: Kenya: Ruto nominates Lydia Chelagat as Data Commissioner as five state corporations get new chiefs
items.summary: President William Ruto has nominated Lydia Sitienei Chelagat as Data Commissioner and sent her name to the National Assembly for approval, state broadcaster KBC reported. items.title: Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta closes after government pressure
items.summary: Novaya Gazeta, one of the few remaining Russian outlets critical of the war in Ukraine, held its last editorial meeting on Monday and closed its newsroom, Al Jazeera reported. The paper had earlier said it was forced to shut down after Moscow labelled it a "foreign agent".
items.imageAlt: The Novaya Gazeta office in Moscow

items.title: Republican congressman Thomas Massie to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth
items.summary: Republican Representative Thomas Massie said he will force a House vote this week to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of violating the Constitution by waging war on Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation, the BBC reported. items.summary: Meta said it will start using AI age-estimation technology on Instagram this month to find teenagers who give an adult birth date and move them into Teen Accounts, later extending it to Facebook and Threads, Al Jazeera reported.

items.title: Uganda: Lack of finance is slowing the move away from mercury in gold mining

items.imageAlt: The terminal of Kigali International Airport, Rwanda

items.title: Museveni keeps Yunus Kakande and 15 other permanent secretaries in their posts
items.summary: President Yoweri Museveni has retained Hajji Yunus Kakande as Permanent Secretary in the Office of the President, one of 16 permanent secretaries keeping their posts in the latest appointments; Minister for the Presidency Milly Babalanda said the decision shows the President's confidence, Nile Post reported.

items.summary: Serie A side Sassuolo dismissed Alberto Aquilani on 9 November after he was appointed in June, following 6 defeats in their last 7 matches that left them close to the relegation zone; he is the 6th coach sacked in Italy within 11 rounds, L'Équipe and Mundo Deportivo reported.

items.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot on Monday blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps for last month's cyberattack on supermarket fridges, which spoiled fresh produce at around 700 stores, describing it as an attack of unprecedented scale and aggressiveness; he said France wants sanctions at European…

items.summary: Former Real Madrid striker Raúl González, 49, has been appointed manager of Real Oviedo, who play in Spain's 2nd division, signing a contract until June 2028; he replaces Julián Calero, who was sacked on Monday with the club in 9th place, BBC Sport reported.

items.title: Kenya: Duale and WHO review Ebola response after 3 weeks without a new case
items.summary: Kenya's Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale met a World Health Organization (WHO) delegation led by its Regional Director for Africa to review Kenya's response to the imported Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, as the country recorded 3 consecutive weeks without a new confirmed case, KBC (state broadcaster) reported.
items.imageAlt: Aden Duale, now Kenya's Health Cabinet Secretary (September 2023 photo)

items.summary: Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsí, 19, has been named Golden Boy 2026, the award for Europe's best under-21 player given by Italian newspaper Tuttosport, ahead of Yan Diomande and Warren Zaire-Emery; he is the 5th Barcelona player to win it after Messi, Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal, Mundo Deportivo and Sky Sport Italia…
items.imageAlt: Pau Cubarsí playing in Argentina vs Spain, the 2026 World Cup final

items.summary: President Donald Trump on Monday asked on his Truth Social platform whether anyone believes this election was honest, without offering evidence, after Democrats retook both chambers of Congress; on election night he had told the New York Times he was absolutely willing to accept the results, the BBC and Türkiye Today…

items.title: Tanzania: New mineral survey uses drones and low-flying aircraft
items.summary: The Geological Survey of Tanzania (GST) has officially launched a modern mineral exploration programme using specialised drones and low-flying aircraft, Minerals Minister Anthony Mavunde announced in Mirerani, where the survey will determine the extent of the tanzanite belt, Daily News (state-owned newspaper) reported.

items.summary: Kenya's Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi called for a law linking the performance and productivity of public servants to their promotions, saying performance contracts cannot be a mere ritual but must become a legal obligation, KBC (state broadcaster) reported.

items.summary: Finnish airline Finnair said a data leak in the global Amadeus booking system may affect up to 116,000 flight bookings of its customers, Sweden Herald reported.

items.summary: Somalia's Defence Minister Ahmed Moalim Fiqi received China's ambassador Wang Yu in Mogadishu, and they discussed defence cooperation, the fight against Al-Shabaab and the future of the AUSSOM mission, Hiiraan Online and Goobjoog reported.

items.summary: Google, part of the Alphabet group, has unveiled two new versions of its artificial intelligence chips known as TPUs (tensor processing units), expanding its competition with Nvidia, Sweden Herald reported.

items.title: Trump says dislike of Israel was among reasons Republicans were defeated
items.summary: President Donald Trump said in an interview with CBS's "60 Minutes" that the Iran war, rising fuel prices and a dislike of Israel were among the reasons Republicans lost the midterm elections, CNN reported.
items.imageAlt: President Donald Trump during a 60 Minutes interview (2025)

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh attends the COP31 climate summit in Antalya
items.summary: Somalia's President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud is attending the 31st UN climate change conference (COP31), which opened on Monday in the Turkish city of Antalya, Hiiraan Online reported.
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud speaking at a gathering in London, May 2013

items.title: Alisson says he wants to stay at Liverpool
items.summary: Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson, whose contract expires at the end of this season, said his wish is to stay at Anfield, after Sunday's 3-1 win at Crystal Palace, Sky Sports reported.
items.imageAlt: Goalkeeper Alisson playing for Brazil in a 2018 friendly

items.title: Uganda: Central bank holds interest rate at 12%
items.summary: The Bank of Uganda kept its Central Bank Rate (CBR) at 12%, warning that energy prices, shilling depreciation and bad weather could push inflation higher, Governor Michael Atingi-Ego said. The bank also widened the CBR band to 3 percentage points.
items.imageAlt: Bank of Uganda building in Kampala

items.title: Kenya: Ruto mocks opposition leaders claiming millions of votes
items.summary: President William Ruto questioned claims by Rigathi Gachagua, Kalonzo Musyoka and Fred Matiang'i that they command millions of votes, after a meeting they held in Nairobi this week about the 2027 election, Capital FM reported. Ruto made the remarks during a tour of the Gusii region.
items.imageAlt: President William Ruto addressing residents in Meru County

items.title: Greece: At least 21 migrants die trying to reach Crete
items.summary: Greece's coastguard said at least 21 people died trying to reach the island of Crete, while more than 100 people were rescued in several operations off the south of the island, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Hellenic Coast Guard office at the port of Heraklion, Crete

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh opens new Hirshabelle buildings in Jowhar
items.summary: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud on Monday opened the new headquarters of the Hirshabelle House of Representatives and the state's Ministry of Security in Jowhar, Goobjoog News reported.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of the town of Jowhar and the surrounding farmland

items.title: Hassan Ali Khaire accuses two officers of killings and land grabbing in Raadeerka, Deyniile
items.summary: Former Somali Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire used his Facebook page to condemn what he called a massacre, land grabbing and forced displacement in the Raadeerka neighbourhood of Deyniile district, blaming two officers he named. Neither the officers nor the government has yet responded to the accusations.
items.imageAlt: A composite image circulated on social media showing two police officers said to be the officers named by Hassan Ali Khaire

items.title: Cricket: England open door for Brydon Carse return and drop Shoaib Bashir
items.summary: England named Brydon Carse in the Lions squad, opening the way for his return to Tests on the South Africa tour, while in the 15-man squad for the 3-Test series starting in Johannesburg on 17 December Liam Patterson-White replaced Shoaib Bashir, BBC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: England cricketer Brydon Carse

items.title: Kenya: Murkomen urges Sifuna to back Ruto, promising leadership in 2032
items.summary: Kenya's Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen urged Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna to drop his presidential ambitions for the 2027 election and back President William Ruto, saying the Luhya community could then take the country's leadership in 2032, Capital FM reported.
items.imageAlt: Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, 2024

items.title: Pierre Kalulu to miss France's Nations League matches through injury
items.summary: Tests carried out after Juventus' match against Fiorentina showed that defender Pierre Kalulu has a muscle injury in his left leg, so he will not take part in France's matches against Italy and Turkey, La Gazzetta dello Sport and L'Équipe reported.
items.imageAlt: Defender Pierre Kalulu, 2022

items.title: South Sudan: Gen. Joseph Lagu to be buried at the Dr John Garang Mausoleum in Juba
items.summary: The organising committee for the state funeral of General Joseph Lagu Yanga, leader of the Anyanya One movement, told Eye Radio that he will be buried inside the Dr John Garang Mausoleum in Juba, after President Salva Kiir decided he should receive a state funeral.
items.imageAlt: General Joseph Lagu arriving at the Dr John Garang Mausoleum site in Juba, 9 July 2011

items.title: Judo legend Teddy Riner to run for French president in 2027
items.summary: Teddy Riner, who has won 5 Olympic gold medals, announced on Monday that he will run in France's 2027 presidential election, France 24 reported.
items.imageAlt: Teddy Riner, the French judo legend

items.title: Trump: "We won in Iran", as US forces strike Qeshm Island
items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Sunday that the United States has "won" the Iran war and that renewed fighting is unlikely if Tehran reaches a deal, as US forces struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, Euronews reported.
items.imageAlt: President Donald Trump in the Oval Office

items.title: Uganda: CAA chief engineer and 10 others in court over vandalism at Entebbe airport
items.summary: 11 officials of the Uganda Civil Aviation Authority, including chief engineer Herbert Ngobi, appeared before the Entebbe High Court on Monday accused of negligence of duty linked to the vandalism of airport installations worth Shs3.7 billion, Nile Post reported.
items.imageAlt: Entebbe International Airport, Uganda

items.title: Golf: 19-year-old Blades Brown becomes youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years
items.summary: American golfer Blades Brown, 19, won the World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico, beating Ben James on the second play-off hole to become the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years, BBC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: American golfer Blades Brown

items.title: Iran: IAEA inspectors recently visited the Bushehr nuclear plant
items.summary: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) recently visited the Bushehr nuclear power plant, calling it evidence that cooperation with the agency continues, Türkiye Today reported.
items.imageAlt: The Bushehr nuclear power plant, Iran

items.title: Guterres: The world has entered an 'age of climate extremes'
items.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Monday urged leaders gathered at COP31 in Antalya to speed up emissions cuts and the transition away from fossil fuels, saying the world has entered 'a new age of climate extremes', Türkiye Today reported.
items.imageAlt: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres

items.title: Tanzania and WTTC discuss attracting tourism investment in London
items.summary: Tanzania's Minister for Natural Resources and Tourism Dr Ashatu Kijaji met World Travel and Tourism Council (WTTC) chairman Manfredi Lefebvre in London, where they discussed tourism investment and increasing international visitors, the government-owned Daily News reported.
items.imageAlt: Manfredi Lefebvre, WTTC chairman (2015 photo)

items.title: IGAD and Germany hold annual partnership dialogue in Djibouti
items.summary: IGAD and the German government held their annual partnership dialogue on Monday at the IGAD headquarters in Djibouti and reaffirmed their commitment to peace, resilience and regional integration in the Horn of Africa, according to an IGAD statement. The IGAD delegation was led by Executive Secretary Dr Workneh…
items.imageAlt: IGAD Executive Secretary Workneh Gebeyehu (2018 photo)

items.title: Ethiopia opens its pavilion at COP31 in Antalya as it prepares to host COP32
items.summary: Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos and Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa opened Ethiopia's pavilion at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, as the country prepares to host COP32 in 2027, reported Fana, which is affiliated with the government.
items.imageAlt: Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos

items.title: Speaker Wetang'ula steps up Ruto re-election campaign in western Kenya
items.summary: Kenya's National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula urged people in western Kenya to back President William Ruto's bid for a second term in the 2027 general election, saying the alliance would strengthen the region's influence in government, KBC reported.
items.imageAlt: Kenya's National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula

items.title: Nairobi extends water rationing after levels fall at Ndakaini Dam
items.summary: Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company said water rationing has been extended because production at the Ngethu and Kigoro treatment plants has fallen by 35% after water levels dropped at Ndakaini Dam; parts of Kiambu, Kajiado and Machakos will also be affected, KBC reported.
items.imageAlt: The Ndakaini reservoir near Thika, Kenya

items.title: Museveni urges Ugandan universities to prioritise practical skills training
items.summary: President Yoweri Museveni urged Ugandan universities to focus on practical skills training so that students can create jobs, saying unemployment is a major challenge; the speech was read at Bugema University by Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja, Nile Post reported.
items.imageAlt: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni

items.title: Bank of Tanzania guarantees unlock 2.1 trillion shillings in loans
items.summary: The Bank of Tanzania (BoT) said it has issued credit guarantees worth 1.6 trillion shillings, helping businesses obtain loans totalling 2.1 trillion shillings across various sectors of the economy, the government-owned Daily News reported.
items.imageAlt: Headquarters of the Bank of Tanzania in Dar es Salaam

items.title: USA and Pacific Islands to host 2030 Rugby League World Cup
items.summary: International Rugby League (IRL) has decided the 2030 World Cup will be held in the USA and the Pacific Islands, with the 5 host cities yet to be announced, BBC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: The Rugby League World Cup trophy on display

items.title: Netherlands: Vitesse v De Graafschap called off after fans block their team's bus
items.summary: A Dutch second-tier match between Vitesse Arnhem and De Graafschap was called off after De Graafschap supporters stopped their own team's bus from leaving for the game, BBC Sport reported.
items.imageAlt: The GelreDome stadium in Arnhem, Netherlands

items.title: Kenyan police seize 454 kg of methamphetamine
items.summary: Kenyan police say they seized 454 kg of methamphetamine worth an estimated $27 million on the country's coast and arrested 3 suspects, the BBC reported.
items.imageAlt: A sample of crystal methamphetamine (illustrative photo)

items.title: Trump says he will meet Putin and Xi in China
items.summary: President Donald Trump said he expects to meet Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen on 18–19 November, saying they would discuss nuclear disarmament and ending the Iran war, Euronews reported.
items.imageAlt: Xi Jinping during the welcome ceremony for Donald Trump in China, May 2026

items.title: Huckabee: US aid to Israel will not be cut off abruptly
items.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee said Washington's $4 billion in aid would not be cut off suddenly, since ending it requires approval from Congress, Türkiye Today reported, citing i24NEWS.
items.imageAlt: Mike Huckabee speaking in Des Moines, Iowa

items.title: Law Society of Kenya demands accountability as lawyer Abshir remains missing
items.summary: The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) has called on security agencies to say where lawyer Abshir Ahmedsadak Abdi is, and announced new demonstrations on Tuesday, the day the High Court at Milimani is due to rule on the habeas corpus case.
items.imageAlt: Kenya's judiciary building in Nairobi

items.title: Tanzania: STAMICO opens 3.7 billion shilling clean fuel factory in Dodoma
items.summary: Tanzania's State Mining Corporation (STAMICO) has opened the Rafiki Briquettes factory in Dodoma, costing 3.7 billion shillings, to reduce reliance on firewood and charcoal, the government-owned Daily News reported.
items.imageAlt: Central Dodoma, Tanzania

items.title: Krakow: Suspected gunman who killed 6 people dies in hospital
items.summary: Polish police said the 24-year-old man suspected of killing at least 6 people in a shooting in central Krakow on Saturday died in hospital early on Monday, the BBC reported.
items.imageAlt: The Town Hall Tower and Cloth Hall on Krakow's Main Market Square

items.title: TikTok removes more than 750,000 videos in Kenya
items.summary: TikTok said it removed 750,185 videos in Kenya that violated its community guidelines between April and June 2026, Capital FM reported.
items.imageAlt: The TikTok app on a mobile phone

items.title: Vodacom Tanzania profit rises 183 percent
items.summary: Vodacom Tanzania said its net profit reached 117.8 billion shillings in the six months to September 2026, while service revenue rose 20.8 percent to 1.067 trillion shillings, The Citizen reported.
items.imageAlt: An M-Pesa agent in Tanzania

items.title: Asian stock markets rebound after tech sell-off
items.summary: Asian stock markets rose on Monday after last week's fall linked to the Democratic Party's victory in the US midterm elections, with Tokyo's Nikkei 225 up 3.45%, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: The Tokyo Stock Exchange building in Japan

items.title: Rubio: War on Iran is unpopular but was necessary to stop the nuclear threat
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday that President Trump launched the war on Iran to protect the world from Tehran's nuclear ambitions, adding that talks are not close to a breakthrough, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Marco Rubio speaking at an event

items.title: Somalia, Egypt and Djibouti say Red Sea security belongs to the coastal states
items.summary: The foreign ministers of Somalia, Egypt and Djibouti pledged on Monday in Tripoli, Libya, that securing the Red Sea is the responsibility of the states on its coasts, Goobjoog News reported.
items.imageAlt: Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, February 2025

items.title: Mexico arrests man suspected of being a senior leader of the Jalisco drug cartel
items.summary: Mexico's Navy said Rafael Alvarez, known as "R2", who is suspected of heading a cell of the CJNG cartel, was arrested on Sunday in the city of Zapopan using intelligence provided by the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Omar García Harfuch, Mexico's security minister

items.title: New Delhi engulfed by toxic smog after Diwali celebrations
items.summary: A cloud of smoke and pollution covered India's capital on Monday morning after people set off firecrackers on Sunday to celebrate Diwali, with the air quality index (AQI) exceeding 350 in many parts of the city, AP reported.
items.imageAlt: Smog covering the sky over Delhi

items.title: Drone attack hits industrial area in Russia's Kirishi
items.summary: Leningrad Region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Telegram that drones attacked an industrial area in the city of Kirishi, about 150 km from St. Petersburg, overnight, and that 113 drones were shot down, the TT news agency reported via Sweden Herald.
items.imageAlt: The KINEF company office in Kirishi, Russia

items.title: Moldova launches new power line to Romania to reduce reliance on Russia
items.summary: Moldova on Sunday officially launched a new power line linking the country to Romania and the European electricity grid, Al Jazeera reported, with the aim of reducing its reliance on Russian energy.
items.imageAlt: Moldovan President Maia Sandu

items.title: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris; Europe to press the US on Ukraine and Iran
items.summary: G7 foreign ministers begin 2 days of talks in Paris on Monday, and France 24 reported that European countries will press the United States to seek a fair settlement for Ukraine and to refrain from new strikes on Iran.
items.imageAlt: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio

items.title: Trump says offering Dana White the press secretary job was a joke
items.summary: President Donald Trump told The New York Times that his offer of the White House press secretary job to UFC chief Dana White was not serious, saying "I was just kidding", Sweden Herald reported, citing the TT news agency.
items.imageAlt: Dana White, head of the UFC

items.title: Biden: Cancer will limit the conversations I can have about my book
items.summary: Former US President Joe Biden said on social media on Sunday that his cancer will prevent him from doing as many conversations promoting his memoir as he had hoped, CNN reported.
items.imageAlt: Portrait of Joe Biden, former President of the United States

items.title: Hakeem Jeffries backs impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
items.summary: US House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said he fully supports a resolution seeking to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, whom he accused of engineering the war in Iran, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of Hakeem Jeffries, Democratic leader in the US House of Representatives

items.title: Merz to name Ilse Aigner as presidential candidate, Germany's first woman head of state if elected
items.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Sunday he will nominate Ilse Aigner, speaker of the Bavarian state parliament, as the CDU and CSU candidate for German president, Al Jazeera reported; if elected, she would be the country's first female head of state.
items.imageAlt: Ilse Aigner, speaker of the Bavarian state parliament

items.title: COP31 climate summit opens today in Antalya; Aliyev to attend
items.summary: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev will attend the UN climate summit COP31, held from 9 to 20 November in the city of Antalya, the first that Türkiye has hosted, Türkiye Today reported.
items.imageAlt: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev

items.title: Trump says he did not know his wealth grew by 3 billion dollars
items.summary: President Donald Trump told CBS News' 60 Minutes that he did not know his wealth had grown by 3 billion dollars since he returned to office, saying a son of his handles his finances, Türkiye Today reported.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of President Donald Trump

items.title: Pope Leo XIV, in Buenos Aires, urges Milei to safeguard democracy
items.summary: In his first speech in Buenos Aires, Pope Leo XIV called on President Javier Milei and Argentina's politicians to safeguard democracy and to use their words carefully, CNN reported.
items.imageAlt: Pope Leo XIV waving to the crowd

items.title: Trump offers UFC chief Dana White the job of White House press secretary
items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Truth Social on Saturday that he had offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, head of the UFC, Al Jazeera reported; White is expected to meet Trump on Monday to discuss it.
items.imageAlt: Dana White, head of the UFC

items.title: Araghchi: Mediators on Iran-US peace deal have stopped travelling
items.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told state television on Sunday that mediators working on a peace deal between Iran and the United States have stopped travelling since the US midterm elections, which he described as a "shock". He said it would take time before the atmosphere is right for the trips to resume,…
items.imageAlt: Abbas Araghchi meeting Rafael Grossi, director of the IAEA, in Vienna

items.title: Leeds United condemn online racist abuse aimed at Jayden Bogle
items.summary: Leeds United have condemned "disgusting" online racist abuse directed at defender Jayden Bogle after Saturday's 1-0 win over Tottenham, BBC Sport reported. Bogle was accused over a tackle on Mathys Tel that the referee did not punish after a VAR review, and Tottenham said they will submit a formal complaint.
items.imageAlt: Elland Road, the stadium of Leeds United, in the city of Leeds

items.title: Somalia and Libya hold talks on strengthening economic and financial cooperation
items.summary: Somalia's Foreign Minister Abdisalam Ali met Libya's Finance Minister Rashid Abu Qaffah in Tripoli, where they discussed strengthening economic and financial cooperation and increasing Somalia's live-animal exports.
items.imageAlt: Somali Foreign Minister Abdisalam Ali and Libyan Finance Minister Rashid Abu Qaffah shaking hands in Tripoli

items.title: Trump: Renewed attacks on Iran "highly unlikely" if talks make progress
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said in a phone interview with CNN on Sunday that it is "highly unlikely" the US will return to war with Iran as long as there is progress in talks on its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. He said it depends on whether Iran signs "a very strong agreement".
items.imageAlt: US President Donald Trump giving an interview, photo from 2025

items.title: South Sudan: Dispute over SPLM primary elections in Greater Pibor
items.summary: A group of delegates of the ruling SPLM has accused the primary election committee in the Greater Pibor Administrative Area of bias and of backing a particular candidate, Radio Tamazuj reported. The process, which had run for about 2 weeks, was suspended on Friday, with officials citing "technical challenges".
items.imageAlt: A view of Pibor, South Sudan

items.title: Erdoğan joins Aliyev for Azerbaijan's Victory Day commemorations in Karabakh
items.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan attended Azerbaijan's 6th Victory Day commemorations in Karabakh on Sunday at the invitation of President Ilham Aliyev, Euronews reported. At a joint press conference, Aliyev said the unity of the two countries "will last forever".
items.imageAlt: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev, photo from 2025

items.title: Russia says it hit power substations and 3 Ukraine-bound ships; hundreds of thousands without power
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said overnight strikes hit 3 cargo ships it accused of carrying weapons for Ukraine and 2 electricity substations, The Moscow Times reported. France 24 said hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians were left without power on Sunday after Russian strikes on energy infrastructure.
items.imageAlt: A darkened street in Kyiv after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, November 2022

items.title: Norway: Fans injured after part of the stand gives way at Tromsø stadium
items.summary: Several fans were injured, one of whom was taken to hospital, after part of the away section at Tromsø's stadium gave way during Sunday's match against Bodø/Glimt, both clubs said, Al Jazeera reported. The match was stopped shortly before half-time.
items.imageAlt: Alfheim Stadium in Tromsø, Norway

items.title: Egypt: Death toll from Giza train collision rises to 4, with 88 injured
items.summary: Egypt's health ministry said at least 4 people were killed and nearly 90 injured when two trains collided in Giza province near Cairo, CNN and Euronews reported. Earlier reports had put the number of injured at 64 with no confirmed deaths.
items.imageAlt: A train of the Egyptian National Railways (ENR)

items.title: Amsterdam: Tens of thousands march to demand Dutch government action against Israel
items.summary: Tens of thousands of people, many dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam on Sunday, pressing the Dutch government to take tougher action against Israel over Gaza, the Associated Press reported.
items.imageAlt: Dam Square in central Amsterdam, with the Royal Palace and the Nieuwe Kerk

items.title: Juba: City authorities review security operations in neighbourhoods and markets
items.summary: Juba city authorities are reviewing security operations in neighbourhoods and markets, focusing on young people engaged in unauthorised brokering and on improving public order, Eye Radio reported.
items.imageAlt: A market in Juba, the capital of South Sudan

items.title: England await results of Marc Guehi injury scan ahead of Nations League matches
items.summary: Manchester City defender Marc Guehi will have a scan on a hip complaint on Sunday to determine whether he can join up with England this week, BBC Sport reported. The 26-year-old was substituted at half-time of City's defeat by Nottingham Forest on Saturday.
items.imageAlt: Marc Guehi in England's match against Panama at the 2026 World Cup

items.title: Poland: Terror investigation opened into Krakow shooting, two days of national mourning declared
items.summary: Poland on Sunday opened a terrorism investigation into Saturday's shooting on Krakow's Main Square in which 6 people were killed, and declared two days of national mourning, France 24 and AP reported. Authorities said the 24-year-old suspect was fascinated by far-right ideologies.
items.imageAlt: The Pod Złotą Głową building on the Main Market Square in Kraków's Old Town

items.title: France: Europe will take part in US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
items.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said on Sunday that Europeans will be represented, and France will take part, in the US-mediated Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, France 24 reported.
items.imageAlt: Jean-Noël Barrot, French Minister of Foreign Affairs

items.title: Pope Leo XIV urges men to respect their wives amid femicide crisis in Latin America
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday urged men to treat their wives with respect as he wrapped up the first leg of his 12-day tour of Latin America, France 24 reported. The region has recorded nearly 20,000 women killed because of their gender over the past five years.
items.imageAlt: Pope Leo XIV on the balcony of Saint Peter's Basilica after his election in 2025

items.title: Egypt: 64 injured in train crash south of Cairo
items.summary: Two trains collided on Sunday in the al-Ayyat district of Giza province, south of Cairo, injuring 64 people, according to Egypt's Ministry of Health. The Egyptian Railway Authority said emergency teams and cranes were sent to clear the wreckage.
items.imageAlt: A train of the Egyptian National Railways (ENR) at Alexandria station

items.title: South Sudan: Inter-party election dialogue to resume on Monday to adopt resolutions
items.summary: South Sudan's political party leaders have agreed to reconvene in Juba on Monday, 9 November, to finalise and adopt the resolutions of the election-related dialogue ahead of the December 2026 general elections, the Office of the SPLM Secretary-General said. The date of the closing ceremony will be set in consultation…
items.imageAlt: Dr Akol Paul Kordit, Secretary General of the SPLM party in South Sudan

items.title: Lionel Messi becomes first player to win the MLS Golden Boot in two consecutive seasons
items.summary: Inter Miami's Lionel Messi scored 26 goals in 31 games, becoming the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons, Nile Post reported, citing BBC Sport. The 39-year-old Messi also provided 17 assists.
items.imageAlt: Lionel Messi playing for Inter Miami (2025)

items.title: Museveni urges Italian investors to invest in Uganda's industrialisation
items.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni met a delegation of more than 80 people from Italy in Entebbe and urged them to invest in coffee factories and lithium batteries, Nile Post reported. Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja said Italy has allocated 120 million euros to Uganda's coffee sector, and a development cooperation…
items.imageAlt: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni

items.title: US forms task force to block Iran's land supply routes
items.summary: US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it has created a new task force, Task Force Iron Gate, aimed at stopping weapons and sanctioned goods moving across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM also said 147 commercial vessels have been redirected since July, while Iranian media reported explosions on Qeshm…
items.imageAlt: The Strait of Hormuz seen from near Bandar Abbas, Iran

items.title: Canary island of El Hierro declares emergency after rise in migrant arrivals
items.summary: Authorities on the Spanish island of El Hierro declared an emergency and asked the government in Madrid for help after more than 3,300 migrants arrived on about 30 boats since the start of November, local officials said. The island has about 11,400 residents.
items.imageAlt: The coastal village of La Restinga, on the island of El Hierro

items.title: La Liga: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 at the Mestalla
items.summary: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 at the Mestalla on Saturday, with goals from Federico Valverde, Arda Güler and Kylian Mbappé, Yahoo Sports reported, a result also confirmed by VAVEL. The win, their eighth in a row, put Real Madrid level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona.
items.imageAlt: The Mestalla stadium in Valencia

items.title: Israel's president picks Gadi Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form the next government
items.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, with forming the next government after 67 lawmakers backed him while Netanyahu received 46, Al Jazeera reported. Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14 days, to secure at least 61 of the Knesset's 120 seats.
items.imageAlt: Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party

items.title: France: more than 140,000 people protest against the rising cost of living
items.summary: France's Interior Ministry said about 146,000 people, 46,000 of them in Paris, protested nationwide on Saturday against the rising cost of living, while unions put the figure at 250,000. Police used tear gas in Paris and Lyon, in the fourth consecutive weekend of protests.
items.imageAlt: An earlier demonstration in the streets of Paris (2023)

items.title: Tennis: Carlos Alcaraz beats Casper Ruud, will face Ben Shelton in the Paris Masters final
items.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Casper Ruud 6-4, 6-4 in the Paris Masters semi-finals, while Ben Shelton beat Luca Van Assche 5-7, 6-3, 6-4, ESPN reported, results also confirmed by the ATP Tour. Alcaraz said he wants revenge against Shelton after losing their last meeting at the US Open.
items.imageAlt: Carlos Alcaraz playing at Roland Garros 2025

items.title: US offers a reward of up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear programme
items.summary: The US State Department's Rewards for Justice programme announced a reward of up to $20 million, and possible relocation, for anyone providing information about Iran's nuclear programme, the BBC reported. Iran insists its programme is peaceful and that it does not seek a nuclear weapon.
items.imageAlt: The US State Department building in Washington

items.title: Pope Leo XIV holds his first mass in Uruguay during Latin America tour
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated mass on Saturday in the city of Paysandu in western Uruguay, attended by about 40,000 people according to the Vatican, as part of a 12-day tour of Latin America. The visit comes after lung surgery last month, and he travels to Argentina on Sunday.
items.imageAlt: Pope Leo XIV (May 2025)

items.title: Arsenal beat Hull City 1-0 with a late goal from Martin Ødegaard
items.summary: Arsenal beat Hull City 1-0 in the Premier League at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with captain Martin Ødegaard scoring in the 72nd minute after following up a shot from Noni Madueke, BBC Sport and Fox Sports reported.
items.imageAlt: Arsenal's Emirates Stadium in London

items.title: All Blacks beat Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield
items.summary: New Zealand's rugby team beat Scotland 43-21 in Edinburgh on Saturday in the Nations Championship, scoring seven tries to Scotland's three, BBC Sport and the official All Blacks website reported. Scotland, only three points behind at half-time, failed to score in the second half.
items.imageAlt: Murrayfield Stadium in Edinburgh

items.title: Poland: At least 6 people killed in a shooting on Krakow's main market square
items.summary: Krakow police said an armed man driving a car opened fire on Saturday on people in the city's main market square, killing at least 6 people and wounding 15 others, CNN reported. Police said the suspect was shot and injured and taken to hospital.
items.imageAlt: Krakow's Main Market Square (Rynek Główny) and St. Mary's Basilica

items.title: F1: Hamilton and Verstappen to start from the back at the São Paulo Grand Prix
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) and Max Verstappen (Red Bull) will start Sunday's São Paulo Grand Prix from the back of the grid after their cars were fitted with complete new power units, BBC Sport reported. Charles Leclerc received a 10-place penalty and George Russell 5 places.
items.imageAlt: The start-finish straight at the Interlagos circuit in São Paulo, Brazil

items.title: New Zealand election produces no clear winner after a very tight result
items.summary: Preliminary results from Saturday's election show Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party won 42 seats, 19 short of the number needed, while Chris Hipkins' Labour Party won 36, the BBC reported. Both sides are preparing for coalition talks that could take weeks.

items.title: Trump names Stephen Miller White House chief of staff

items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by Yemen's Houthis towards the Medina region, after the civil defence agency warned of danger near the port of Yanbu, Al Jazeera reported. items.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted the death sentences of all 548 people on death row in the state to life in prison, the BBC reported. items.title: Iran says several oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said at least 5 oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, Al Jazeera reported. Iran said one of the vessels struck a mine, as the US and Israeli war on Iran remains unresolved.

items.summary: President Isaias Afwerki met Hu Changchun, China's Special Envoy for Horn of Africa Affairs, in Asmara on 5 November, and they discussed bilateral ties and the situation in the region, Eritrea's Ministry of Information said. items.summary: Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association, announced on Thursday that he will challenge Gianni Infantino in FIFA's presidential election in March, Al Jazeera reported. items.title: Armenia plans to apply for EU membership in 2027 or 2028
items.summary: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said on Thursday that his country would formally submit an application for full European Union membership in 2027 or 2028, Türkiye Today reported.
