items.imageAlt: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan addressing the European Parliament in Strasbourg in 2023

items.title: Hakimi, Mané, Semenyo and Díaz among CAF Awards 2026 nominees
items.summary: Defending winner Achraf Hakimi, Sadio Mané, Antoine Semenyo and Brahim Díaz are on the men's shortlist for the CAF Awards 2026, KBC reported. The awards will be presented on the 7th of next month in Lagos, Nigeria.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from Portugal's national team
items.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, has announced his retirement from Portugal's national team after playing 234 matches and scoring 146 goals since 2003, both world records, BBC Sport reported. In a video posted on Instagram, Ronaldo said the day had come for him to hand back the number 7 shirt.
items.imageAlt: Cristiano Ronaldo in a Portugal shirt during a friendly between Portugal and Argentina in Geneva

items.title: Saudi Arabia and Syria sign a defence cooperation agreement
items.summary: Saudi Arabia and Syria signed a defence cooperation agreement on Wednesday during a visit to Riyadh by Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, the Saudi state news agency SPA reported, as cited by Daily Sabah. Al-Sharaa met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; details of the agreement were not disclosed.
items.imageAlt: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa with President Donald Trump during his visit to Saudi Arabia in 2025

items.title: National strikes and protests take place in France
items.summary: Five trade unions joined a national day of strikes and protests in France, demanding higher wages and protection of public services, the BBC reported. Authorities expected 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators, while Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 70,000 police and gendarmes had been deployed.

items.title: Alan Jones, 1980 Formula 1 champion, dies aged 80
items.summary: Alan Jones, the last Australian and the first Williams driver to win the Formula 1 world championship, has died aged 80, BBC Sport reported. His wife Amanda Butler-Davis said in a statement released by Motorsport Australia that he died on 5 November after a short illness; Jones won 12 Grands Prix.
items.imageAlt: The Williams FW07B in which Alan Jones won the 1980 Formula 1 championship

items.title: Tanzania: High Court to rule on 6 November in Tundu Lissu's case
items.summary: Tanzania's High Court, Dar es Salaam Sub-Registry, will deliver its judgment on 6 November in the treason trial of opposition Chadema party chairman Tundu Lissu, The Citizen reported. A three-judge bench led by Justice Dunstan Ndunguru will decide whether to convict or acquit him.

items.summary: Como, coached by Cesc Fàbregas, won 9-1 at Lens, with Anastasios Douvikas scoring three goals, the Irish Examiner reported. The nine goals equal the most scored by one team in a Champions League match, after Bayern Munich's 9-2 win over Dinamo Zagreb in 2024.

items.title: UN: Gunfire damages tents of displaced people in Rafah
items.summary: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said gunfire hit and damaged several tents at a displacement site in northern Rafah, Gaza, injuring people, UN News reported. Secretary-General's spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said civilians and humanitarian workers must be protected.

items.title: UNCTAD: Developing countries bear the heaviest burden of fuel prices
items.summary: A new UNCTAD report says developing countries have borne the heaviest burden of rising fuel prices after the war closed the Strait of Hormuz in February, UN News reported. For example, diesel in Nigeria rose about 83% between late February and the end of August, while in Ireland it rose 9%.

items.title: Trump: The Iran war affected the election, but I did the right thing
items.summary: President Donald Trump admitted that the attack on Iran and high fuel prices contributed to the Republican Party's midterm losses, but told the Wall Street Journal: "I did the right thing," Al Jazeera reported. Vice President JD Vance wrote on X that the reason for the defeat was the war.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of US Vice President JD Vance

items.title: Somalia adopts a six-month plan to reach unvaccinated children
items.summary: The National Committee for Immunisation and Polio Eradication, chaired by Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre, approved a six-month plan to expand child vaccination, Dawan Africa reported. According to WHO and UNICEF, about 1.5 million Somali children under five have never received a routine vaccine.

items.title: South Africa votes in local council elections seen as a test for the ANC

items.title: Former baseball star Mark Teixeira wins a seat in the US House of Representatives
items.summary: Mark Teixeira, a three-time MLB All-Star, won the seat for Texas's 21st district for the Republican Party, defeating Democrat Kristin Hook, ESPN reported. The seat was previously held by Chip Roy, who did not run again.

items.summary: Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff defeated Republican candidate Mike Collins in the US midterm elections, Al Jazeera reported. With 56% of votes counted, Ossoff had 63% and Collins 29%, according to the AP; which party will control the two chambers of Congress has not yet been announced.

items.summary: Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar was re-elected to the seat for Minnesota's 5th district, which she has represented since 2019, Horseed Media reported. In her victory speech she thanked her supporters, many of whom are Somali.

items.imageAlt: The Arab League headquarters in Cairo

items.title: US to suspend South Africa and Rwanda from AGOA duty-free trade
items.summary: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced that South Africa and Rwanda will be suspended from the AGOA programme from 1 January 2027, saying both countries failed to meet its criteria. South Africa exported goods worth about $1.7 billion under the programme in 2025, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported.
items.imageAlt: Official portrait of US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer (2025)

items.title: Iran says its ceasefire plan with the US can be accelerated
items.summary: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the ceasefire plan Iran proposed to the US can now be implemented in two days instead of seven, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran insisted that the US lift its naval blockade and sanctions, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Abbas Araghchi, now Iran's foreign minister, on a visit to the IAEA (2021)

items.title: Germany: IG Metall union launches strikes over pay
items.summary: The IG Metall union launched strikes at companies including Audi and Mercedes-Benz, demanding a 5% pay rise for about 3.7 million workers. The union rejected the employers' offer, calling it a real-terms pay cut, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported.
items.imageAlt: IG Metall union members on a warning strike in Witten, Germany (2012)

items.title: India says it freed the fishing vessel Azini hijacked off Somalia's Bari coast
items.summary: The Indian government said its navy and air force freed the Iranian-flagged fishing vessel Azini and the 20 crew members on board in a 48-hour operation in the Indian Ocean, Horseed Media reported. The vessel was reportedly hijacked on 29 October between Bandar Beyla and Hafun.
items.imageAlt: Indian Navy warship INS Betwa docked in Mumbai (2009)

items.title: Ukraine: 24 killed in strike on aid centre in Zaporizhzhia region
items.summary: Ukraine's emergency services said 24 people were killed in a bombing blamed on Russia that hit a school used as an aid centre in the village of Komyshuvakha. President Zelenskyy condemned the attack, while Russia has previously denied targeting civilians, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Music school building in the village of Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region (2025)

items.title: France: high school students' protests resume, but on a small scale
items.summary: French high school students resumed their protests after a two-week holiday, but the Education Ministry said only 41 schools were blockaded on Monday, compared with hundreds in previous weeks, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Students blockading the Lycée Buffon in Paris, December 2024

items.title: Abdullah Öcalan moved to a new section of the İmralı island prison
items.summary: Turkey has moved Abdullah Öcalan, the jailed founder of the PKK, to a newly built section of the İmralı island prison, according to lawmakers from the DEM party, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: İmralı island seen from an aircraft

items.title: Brooklyn court begins trial of two MLB players accused in a betting case
items.summary: Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz, who formerly played for the Cleveland Guardians, face a trial in a federal court in Brooklyn in which prosecutors accuse them of taking money from two gamblers; both have pleaded not guilty, Al Jazeera reported, citing AP.
items.imageAlt: The federal courthouse in Brooklyn, New York

items.title: Chinese state TV keeps blacking out Real Madrid matches after the Mbappé row
items.summary: Neither of CCTV's two sports channels showed Real Madrid's 3-0 win over Racing Santander on Sunday, as the row over a video in which Kylian Mbappé spoke about Mao Zedong continues, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP.
items.imageAlt: Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabéu stadium

items.title: Bangladesh: garment workers' protests continue for a third day
items.summary: Hundreds of garment factories in Bangladesh have been disrupted as workers protest low pay and the rising cost of living, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: Women working in a garment factory in Bangladesh

items.title: Hebron governor says Israeli forces have left the city after a 10-day siege
items.summary: Hebron Governor Khaled Dudin said on Monday that Israeli forces had withdrawn from the West Bank city after a 10-day siege and that Palestinian security forces had taken control of the area, Al Jazeera reported.
items.imageAlt: The Old City of Hebron

items.title: NBA: Yaxel Lendeborg scores 37 as the Warriors beat the Clippers 124-112
items.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scored 37 points, the most by a Warriors rookie since Stephen Curry in 2010, ESPN reported.
items.imageAlt: Yaxel Lendeborg playing for Michigan, February 2026

items.title: Puntland enlists troops to be trained by the US at a base in Bosaso
items.summary: Puntland authorities have begun enlisting nearly 100 soldiers from various security units, who will be trained by the United States at a military base in Bosaso, Garowe Online reported, citing local media.
items.imageAlt: General view of the city of Bosaso

items.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history
items.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, 20, finished 3rd at the Mexico City Grand Prix to win the drivers' championship, while Max Verstappen won the race, the FIA said.
items.imageAlt: Kimi Antonelli celebrating after the Chinese Grand Prix (2026)

items.title: Serie A: Juventus beat Napoli 2-0, Lazio go top
items.summary: Juventus beat 10-man Napoli 2-0, while Lazio, who beat Cagliari 2-1, went top of Serie A for the first time in 16 years, Football Italia reported.
items.imageAlt: Juventus's stadium (Allianz Stadium) in Turin, Italy

items.title: Arab Parliament condemns attack on Qatari gas tanker
items.summary: The Arab Parliament strongly condemned the targeting of Qatar's liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier Al Mayeda as it sailed in the Arabian Gulf, warning that such attacks threaten regional security and energy supplies, SONNA reported.
items.imageAlt: The LNG carrier Mozah, owned by Qatar's Nakilat, at Ras Laffan (2010)

items.title: Mogadishu's Erdogan Hospital brings in advanced machines for diagnosing cancer
items.summary: Mogadishu's Recep Tayyip Erdogan Hospital (Digfeer) has added three machines to its tissue pathology department, the first of their kind brought to Somalia, the head of the department, Dr. Ismail Mahmoud Abdullahi, told Dawan Africa.
items.imageAlt: The grounds of Recep Tayyip Erdogan Hospital in Mogadishu (2015)

items.title: Premier League: Arsenal beat Liverpool 1-0 and go top
items.summary: A 16th-minute goal from Kai Havertz gave Arsenal their first win at Anfield in 14 years and moved them to the top of the Premier League, AP reported.
items.imageAlt: Liverpool's Anfield stadium seen from the main stand

items.title: Bundesliga: Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hamburger SV 3-1
items.summary: Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hamburger SV 3-1 and climbed to 8th place in the Bundesliga, Bulinews and IANS reported.
items.imageAlt: An Eintracht Frankfurt match at its Waldstadion (Deutsche Bank Park), 2024

items.title: LaLiga: Real Madrid beat Racing Santander 3-0
items.summary: Real Madrid scored three first-half goals away at Racing Santander to record a sixth straight win, according to reports from the club and ESPN.
items.imageAlt: El Sardinero stadium in Santander, Spain

items.title: SomBank and IBS Bank offer Islamic financing to Somali fishers
items.summary: SomBank says it has provided Somali fishers with Islamic financing of up to $2 million, while IBS Bank has unveiled a new service called “Kalluun Kaabe”, Dawan Africa reported.
items.imageAlt: Two Somali fishermen in the town of Barawe

items.title: Saudi Noor programme launches free eye treatment and surgery in Mogadishu
items.summary: The Saudi Noor 2026 humanitarian programme has launched free eye-care services at Madina Hospital in Mogadishu, expected to reach about 500 patients, Dawan Africa reported.
items.imageAlt: A doctor in the emergency room of Madina Hospital, Mogadishu (2014)

items.title: Ligue 1: Marseille beat Toulouse 2-0 at the Vélodrome
items.summary: Olympique de Marseille beat Toulouse 2-0 in a round 9 Ligue 1 match, Foot Mercato reported.
items.imageAlt: Olympique de Marseille's Vélodrome stadium

items.title: COP17 in Yerevan adopts a plan to speed up action to protect nature
items.summary: Countries attending the UN Biodiversity Conference (COP17) in the Armenian capital agreed the “Yerevan Pathway”, a plan to accelerate work on the 23 targets to be met by 2030, UN News reported.
items.imageAlt: Entrance of the UN Biodiversity Conference (COP17) venue in Yerevan, Armenia

items.title: Mo Ibrahim: democracy and human rights are declining in Africa
items.summary: Mo Ibrahim, founder of the Mo Ibrahim Foundation, told the AFP news agency that democracy and human rights are declining in Africa. The foundation's index showed economic progress but declines in security and public participation.
items.imageAlt: Mo Ibrahim giving a keynote speech in Uppsala, Sweden (2014)

items.title: President Irro receives credentials of Israel's ambassador in Hargeisa
items.summary: According to Dawan Africa, Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi (Irro) on Sunday received, at the presidential palace in Hargeisa, the credentials of Michael Lotem, Israel's ambassador to Somaliland.
items.imageAlt: President Irro speaking with AFRICOM commander Gen. Dagvin Anderson in Hargeisa (November 2025)

items.title: UN mission in Western Sahara (MINURSO) ends after 35 years
items.summary: MINURSO's mandate expired at midnight on Saturday after the Security Council failed to agree on its future. Secretary-General António Guterres said the UN stands ready to keep supporting peace efforts, UN News reported.
items.imageAlt: MINURSO headquarters in Laayoune (2012)

items.title: Bosaso hosts Somalia's first beach soccer tournament
items.summary: According to Dawan Africa, the Puntland Football Association and the Somali Football Federation launched a beach soccer tournament in Bosaso on 30 October with 6 teams taking part, marking the first appearance of women in the event.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of Bosaso and its coastline (2024)

items.title: Somalia takes part in the opening of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games
items.summary: Somalia's flag was among those presented at the opening of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, which run from 31 October to 13 November. Somalia is represented by 17-year-old boxer Hassan Anwar, who competes in the 50-kilogram category.
items.imageAlt: Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games torch relay event in Diamniadio

items.title: Golden State Valkyries win their first WNBA title
items.summary: According to the AP news agency, the Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals to win their first title, in only their 2nd season.
items.imageAlt: Golden State Valkyries playing Indiana Fever (May 2026)

items.title: Lewis Hamilton takes pole for the Mexico City Grand Prix
items.summary: According to Sky Sports, Lewis Hamilton took his first pole position as a Ferrari driver at the Mexico City Grand Prix, ahead of George Russell and Charles Leclerc.
items.imageAlt: Lewis Hamilton driving for Ferrari (2025)

items.title: Canelo Álvarez reclaims WBC super-middleweight title
items.summary: According to Sky Sports, Mexican boxer Canelo Álvarez beat Christian Mbilli, a previously unbeaten champion, by unanimous decision in Riyadh to win back the WBC belt.
items.imageAlt: Canelo Álvarez throws a jab (file photo, 2017)

items.title: Nigeria investigates two suspected Ebola cases
items.summary: According to Al Jazeera, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said two people suspected of having Ebola were identified in the country’s northeast; they have been isolated and laboratory tests are under way.
items.imageAlt: The Ebola virus seen under an electron microscope

items.title: EU investigates reports that an Iranian-owned fishing vessel was hijacked off the Bari coast
items.summary: The European Union's naval operation ATALANTA is investigating reports that pirates hijacked the Iranian-owned fishing vessel Azini on 29 October near Bandarbeyla district. The Maritime Security Centre MSCIO urged merchant ships to remain vigilant.
items.imageAlt: EU badge on a warship taking part in Operation Atalanta (file photo, 2009)

items.title: Somalia and Oman discuss expanding trade and investment
items.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Jamaal Maxamed Xasan met Oman's ambassador to Somalia, Saalim bin Xabiib Al Camiri, in Mogadishu. SONNA reported that the meeting focused on strengthening trade between the two countries and creating new business opportunities.
items.imageAlt: Al Alam Palace in Muscat, Oman

items.title: Somalia and Russia discuss security cooperation and police training
items.summary: Internal Security Minister Cabdullaahi Sheekh Ismaaciil (Fartaag) met Igor Zubov, Russia's Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs. Zubov said his government is ready to share its knowledge and training in fighting crime, Goobjoog reported.
items.imageAlt: Somali police officers in a training exercise at General Kahiye Police Academy, Mogadishu (file photo, 2014)

items.title: Federal government begins planning a 110 km road linking Buuhoodle and Tuulo-Samakaab
items.summary: Horseed Media reported that Minister Ayuub Ismaaciil of the federal government signed the road plan in the presence of MP Cabdi Qawdhan. The MP said the project is a major victory that will change the lives of local residents.
items.imageAlt: The town of Buuhoodle (file photo, 2015)

items.title: Barcelona thrash Alavés 6-1 as Lamine Yamal scores 2
items.summary: According to ESPN, Barcelona beat Alavés 6-1 at the Spotify Camp Nou and returned to the top of La Liga.
items.imageAlt: Lamine Yamal on the pitch (2025)

items.title: Bayern and Dortmund draw 2-2 as Harry Kane misses a penalty
items.summary: According to ESPN, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund drew 2-2 at the Allianz Arena in the Bundesliga's Der Klassiker.
items.imageAlt: Bayern Munich's Allianz Arena (file photo)

items.title: AC Milan beat Inter 3-1 in the Milan derby
items.summary: According to ESPN, AC Milan beat Inter 3-1 at San Siro, ending Inter's run of 9 league games without defeat.
items.imageAlt: Milan's San Siro stadium (file photo)

items.title: Washington DC and Virginia sue to block Trump’s triumphal arch
items.summary: According to Al Jazeera, Washington DC and the state of Virginia have asked a federal court to stop President Trump’s plan to build a triumphal arch at Memorial Circle, calling it unlawful.
items.imageAlt: The Arlington Memorial Bridge over the Potomac River, Washington, D.C.

items.title: Erdogan urges Russia and Ukraine to stop Black Sea attacks
items.summary: According to Al Jazeera, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, speaking in Istanbul alongside President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea are unacceptable, whoever carries them out.
items.imageAlt: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan (2025)

items.title: Electoral commission opens registration of political organisations ahead of the 2027 elections
items.summary: According to Dawan Africa, registration of political organisations will run from 1 to 22 November. Somalia is preparing for parliamentary elections in April 2027 and a presidential election in May 2027.
items.imageAlt: Logo of the National Independent Electoral Commission

items.title: President Deni rejects the 2027 election timetable and calls for an interim council
items.summary: Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni told Puntland television he does not see an election that Hassan Sheikh can organise, and called for an interim council to lead the country to elections. Dawan Africa noted that the allegations he made have not been independently verified.
items.imageAlt: Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni speaking at the National Consultative Council in Mogadishu (2021)

items.title: Brighton beat Manchester City 1-0 away
items.summary: According to Al Jazeera, Yasin Ayari scored the only goal in the 11th minute as Brighton won at City’s ground for the first time, at the 18th attempt.
items.imageAlt: The Amex Stadium, home of Brighton, England (2013)

items.title: South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs to win the Test series
items.summary: According to Al Jazeera, South Africa won the 3rd Test at Newlands to take the series 2-1, after Australia, set 288 to win, were bowled out for 111.
items.imageAlt: Newlands Cricket Ground, Cape Town

items.title: Chelsea beat Manchester United 2-0 as United go 9 games without a win
items.summary: According to Sky Sports, Chelsea beat Manchester United 2-0 at Stamford Bridge after Lisandro Martínez was sent off in the 63rd minute.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of Chelsea's Stamford Bridge stadium, London (2023)

items.title: Somaliland warns against abuses targeting Ethiopian residents of Borama
items.summary: Somaliland's Information Minister, Barkhad Jaamac Batuun, said abuse or intimidation of foreigners will not be tolerated. He said no one has the right to forcibly expel or attack a foreigner and that such matters will go through legal procedures, Dawan Africa reported.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of the town of Borama (2024)

items.title: US Coast Guard adds Somalia to list of ports failing security standards
items.summary: According to Garowe Online, the US Coast Guard said in a notice that Somalia's ports lack effective anti-terrorism measures. The decision, which took effect on 27 October, means additional security checks for ships bound for the United States after calling at Somali ports.
items.imageAlt: Shipping containers at the port of Mogadishu (file photo, 2015)

items.title: Achraf Hakimi scores a hat-trick as PSG beat Le Havre 5-1
items.summary: According to ESPN, PSG beat Le Havre 5-1 on Friday, with Moroccan defender Achraf Hakimi scoring 3 goals and setting up 2 more.
items.imageAlt: Achraf Hakimi in a Morocco shirt (2024)

items.title: Somaliland bans civilians from carrying firearms
items.summary: According to Dawan Africa, Somaliland police chief Abdirahman Abdullahi said security forces have been ordered to confiscate weapons from people who do not hold a permit.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of Hargeisa (2022)

items.title: Mogadishu marks the 103rd anniversary of the Republic of Türkiye
items.summary: The Turkish Embassy in Mogadishu held a ceremony for the 103rd anniversary of the founding of the Republic of Türkiye. Upper House Speaker Abdi Hashi Abdullahi said relations between the two countries are built on friendship and mutual respect, recalling Erdoğan's 2011 visit.
items.imageAlt: The Turkish embassy in Mogadishu

items.title: Uganda begins withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly 20 years
items.summary: Uganda's army chief, Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, said the withdrawal of UPDF troops from Somalia has begun and that security is being handed over to Somali forces. Garowe Online said the move comes as funding for support to the AUSSOM mission has been cut.
items.imageAlt: Ugandan troops serving with the African Union mission in Somalia mount a guard of honour (file photo, 2021)

items.title: Heritage Institute publishes a study on the role of civil society in Somalia
items.summary: According to Dawan Africa, the Heritage Institute for Policy Studies has released a study assessing the role, effectiveness and challenges of civil society organisations in Somalia, particularly their contribution to transparency and government accountability. The institute's director, Mursal Maxamuud Saney, said…
items.imageAlt: Members of civil society groups at a town hall meeting in Mogadishu (file photo, 2014)

items.title: Gen. Mohamed Ali Barise formally takes command of the Somali National Army
items.summary: Dawan Africa reported that Gen. Barise, who was appointed on 25 October, took over from Gen. Madey Nuuray Sheikh Ufurow. Barise previously held the post from 2019 to 2020.
items.imageAlt: Somali National Army soldiers taking part in a military parade (2013)

items.title: Petroleum Authority: Curad-1 offshore oil well has reached a key layer
items.summary: The chairman of the Somali Petroleum Authority said drilling of the Curad-1 well, led by Turkish company TPAO, has reached a layer where signs of oil could appear. He said the final target is expected to be reached in December.
items.imageAlt: Turkish drilling ship Kanuni (2020), not the Çağrı Bey

items.title: Somaliland bans its residents from taking part in Somali politics
items.summary: Somaliland's Ministry of Interior issued an order saying that anyone who takes part in Somalia's political activities may face legal action. The order did not specify which activities it covers or how it will be enforced.
items.imageAlt: The House of Representatives building in Hargeisa (file photo, 2015)

items.title: UN mission ends without a mechanism to resolve the election dispute
items.summary: The United Nations political mission ends on Saturday without agreement on an alternative mechanism to mediate the dispute over the president's term of office. President Hassan Sheikh has invited the opposition to talks on 14–18 November, but the main opposition groups have not yet confirmed their participation.
items.imageAlt: A UN Security Council meeting on the situation in Somalia (file photo, 2019)

items.title: Hirshabelle approves a $47.45 million budget for 2027
items.summary: Dawan Africa reported that Hirshabelle's council of ministers, chaired by President Gudlawe, approved the 2027 budget, which is 7% larger than the 2026 budget. The meeting also discussed security, elections and flood preparedness.
items.imageAlt: Map of Somalia showing Hirshabelle state

items.title: House of the People suspends sessions for two weeks to install the E-Parliament system
items.summary: Speaker of the House of the People Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur said sessions will be suspended from 31 October. He said the new system will introduce electronic voting and digital registration.
items.imageAlt: Federal MPs seated at a parliamentary ceremony (2016)

items.title: Somalia prepares for El Niño floods feared to worsen food shortages
items.summary: According to Goobjoog, the World Food Programme (WFP) and partner agencies are strengthening emergency plans, including early warning, transport routes and cash assistance, ahead of the El Niño rains. Riverside communities were described as the most at risk.
items.imageAlt: Satellite image showing flooding along the Shabelle River

items.title: EU: Somali goods can enter its markets duty-free
items.summary: The EU delegation to Somalia said Somalia is one of 33 African countries that the 'Everything But Arms' scheme allows to export goods, except arms, to Europe duty-free. Goobjoog noted that the benefit depends on traders meeting European quality standards.
items.imageAlt: The port of Berbera, an export hub (2023)

items.title: Turkey says it will send a research and fishing vessel to Somalia's coast
items.summary: Turkish Ambassador to Somalia Ferhat Alkan announced, during National Fisheries Week in Mogadishu, that a research and fishing vessel will be sent to strengthen the skills of Somali fishermen. The vessel's name and arrival date have not been disclosed.
items.imageAlt: Fishing boats and nets on the shore at Garacad

items.title: Ethiopia says it has received 12 fighter jets from Russia
items.summary: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced that Ethiopia has received 12 Su-35 aircraft and is awaiting S-400 air defence systems, amid tension on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border.
items.imageAlt: A Su-35 fighter jet

items.title: Energy minister blames rising Mogadishu electricity prices on fuel costs
items.summary: Minister Abdullahi Bidhaan said the increase in electricity prices in Mogadishu resulted from fuel price inflation linked to tension in the Middle East, noting that the government had blocked a proposal to double prices.
items.imageAlt: An electricity pole in Mogadishu (file photo, 2015)

items.title: Farmaajo calls for an independent investigation into the Jamea fighting
items.summary: Former President Farmaajo accused the government of using the armed forces in political disputes. The government said 75 Al-Shabaab fighters were killed in the fighting.
items.imageAlt: Former President Farmaajo giving a speech (2017)

items.title: Somalia launches a five-year plan on youth, peace and security
items.summary: The 2026–2030 plan aims to increase the role of young people in peacebuilding.
items.imageAlt: Young people at a youth conference in Mogadishu (file photo, 2016)

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh postpones a planned trip to Russia
items.summary: Somalia's president has postponed the planned trip to Russia. The report linked the decision to Al-Shabaab attacks and election tensions.
items.imageAlt: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud at a meeting (2015)

items.title: Residents take the weapons that were on a bombed vehicle on the outskirts of Buurhakabo
items.imageAlt: Soldiers silhouetted near Buurhakabo at dusk (file photo, 2013)

items.title: African Union forces prepare to withdraw from key bases
items.summary: The troop withdrawal has raised concern about the security situation in Somalia.
items.imageAlt: African Union troops waiting for an aircraft at Mogadishu airport (2011)

items.title: Museveni urges Somalis to unite to defeat Al-Shabaab
items.summary: The President of Uganda said unity is the key to overcoming the biggest challenge facing Somalia.
items.imageAlt: President Museveni welcoming President Hassan Sheikh at the Kampala summit (2023)

items.title: UN political mission in Somalia comes to an end
items.summary: The closure of the mission ends more than thirty years of UN support for peacebuilding and governance.
items.imageAlt: Nicholas Kay, UNSOM's first head, arrives in Mogadishu as the mission begins (2013)

items.title: Villa Somalia formally invites the Opposition Forum to consultations
items.summary: The Opposition Forum, which includes Deni and Ahmed Madobe, and the Nabad iyo Nolol party have been invited to the consultations, which will take place on 14–18 November.
items.imageAlt: Five members of the Madasha forum in a group photo
